Sharp, J.H., Lawrence, C.D. and Yang, R. (1999, reprinted). Calcium sulfoaluminate cements - low-energy cements, special cements or what? In: Dhir, R.K. and Paine, K.A. (eds), ICE Themes Low Carbon Concrete, Chapter 8, pp.143-160. ICE Publishing, London. ISBN 978-0-7277-6459-1. doi:10.1680/icetlcc.64591.143. Reprint of Sharp, J.H., Lawrence, C.D. and Yang, R. (1999). Advances in Cement Research 11(1), 3-13. doi:10.1680/adcr.1999.11.1.3

Book-chapter reprint (ICE Themes Low Carbon Concrete, 2019) of Sharp, Lawrence and Yang 1999, Advances in Cement Research 11(1), 3-13: same title, authors, text, tables and references (the opening says the paper is based on a 1998 lecture and ends "other papers in this issue"). Loaded: SAB and Chinese CSA descriptions, commercial status in China, clinkering temperatures, and (measures) the 25% energy and 40% limestone savings for high-C4A3S cements. Table 1 pure-phase enthalpies and CO2 to other-values. No per-tonne energy, cost, capacity or lifetime. Locators are the book's printed pages 143-160 (PDF page = printed - 142). The book year is not printed in the chapter; 2019 is taken from the PDF creation date (6 Sep 2019) - verify. Figs 1-2 (Gygi) are chart-only. UKERC credits the 1999 original (sharp_1999_001) for its Aether rows C-CS5/C-CS6; recon written against this reprint.
